name: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape

facts.claim: UNESCO World Heritage listed (2019) cultural landscape of the Gunditjmara people, showing how they built an aquaculture system of channels and weirs over thousands of years.
Comprises three components: Budj Bim (northern, including Budj Bim National Park and Lake Condah Mission), Kurtonitj (central) and Tyrendarra (southern).
Visitors can take Gunditjmara-guided cultural tours and visit the Tae Rak Aquaculture Centre and cafe at Lake Condah.
Considered one of Victoria's earliest and largest Indigenous aquaculture ventures, with evidence of eel farming and smoking for food and trade.

name: Mount Eccles National Park

facts.claim: Now officially named Budj Bim National Park (Budj Bim formerly Mount Eccles), co-managed by Parks Victoria and Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners.
Has a tranquil crater lake, lava canals and caves in a bushland setting, with four walking options including the crater rim and lava flow canals.
Manna Gums in the campground are a favourite food of koalas.
Budj Bim is a volcano rising to 178 m in south-west Victoria; the easiest route up is the Lava Canal track.

name: The Horn

facts.claim: The Horn is the highest point in Mount Buffalo National Park at 1,723 m.
A walk leads up from The Horn picnic area to the summit.
Kestrels can be seen diving on Bogong Moths there at sunset.

name: The Gorge (Mount Buffalo)

facts.claim: The Gorge Day Visitor Area has a viewing area looking over the gorge, near Mount Buffalo Chalet.
Visitors come to watch the sunrise from the Gorge above fog in the valleys.
The Gorge - Lake Catani track starts from the Gorge Day Visitor Area.

name: Eurobin Falls

facts.claim: Eurobin Falls is reached by the Eurobin Falls Walk from the Eurobin Falls trailhead and picnic area.
Wildflowers bloom around Eurobin and Rollason's Falls in spring, and the falls run fullest after rain and snowmelt.
Ladies Bath Falls is nearby and Parks Victoria lists both under 'Ladies Bath and Eurobin Falls'.
